extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and molecular/cell biology researchers (K99/R00 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Research strategy for a K99/R00 proposal testing how chromatin modifiers and lipid homeostasis regulate actin form and function during aging using C. elegans (and complementary human cell screens). Includes multi-pronged genetic screens, mechanistic aims, and defined quantitative/qualitative assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tissue-specific quantitative and qualitative actin integrity measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitatively and qualitatively analyze tissue-specific patterns of actin filament structure and integrity using LifeAct-mRuby lines in muscle, intestine, and hypodermis across ages D1, D4, D7, D10, and D13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four specific measurements are proposed that have been characterized in the lab to decline with age and correlate with healthy actin: 1) thickness of muscle actin filaments measured as width of peaks at mid-height across a line profile (see similar quantifications in [21]); 2) integrated fluorescent intensity of hypodermal actin measured using a COPAS large particle biosorter (see similar quantifications in [22]); 3) indirect measurement of intestinal filamentous actin by measuring the ratio of fluorescent intensity of LifeAct localized to filaments versus cytoplasmic signal; and 4) dynamics of actin measured using fluorescent recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) of LifeAct signal in star-like hypodermal actin structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of RNAi phenotypes with CRISPR-Cas9 null mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: All knockdown experiments will be validated in null mutants generated by CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments will first be performed with RNAi (because RNAi knockdown has stronger phenotypes than loss-of-function [lof] mutants, likely due to adaptation across generations), and then validated in corresponding CRISPR nulls to confirm that observed phenotypes are attributable to the targeted gene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifespan and thermal stress survival as physiological readouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether perturbations (knockdown or overexpression) of candidate genes alter organismal lifespan and survival under thermal stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: bet-1 knockdown decreases lifespan and increases heat sensitivity; test whether bet-1 overexpression extends lifespan and whether any lifespan effects depend on intact actin by combining overexpression with RNAi of actin/regulators. Include caveat experiments if overexpression does not extend lifespan (use knockdown/lof instead to test additivity or shared mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-pronged screening to identify candidate regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use complementary, independent screens to identify genes involved in cytoskeletal maintenance: in vivo imaging, whole-genome synthetic lethality RNAi in C. elegans, RNAseq under sub-lethal actin knockdown, and genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening in human BJ fibroblasts under actin stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-referencing hits across these variable datasets is used to prioritize candidates; overlapping functions across screens (e.g., chromatin remodeling and lipid homeostasis) provide high confidence in identified genes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic lethality screen criteria in hsf-1 mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify genes that are essential for survival in hypomorphic or mutant backgrounds of hsf-1 via genome-wide RNAi synthetic lethality screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen details include use of ~10,000 RNAi feeding vectors, scoring for synthetic lethality on RNAi in hsf-1(sy441) truncated protein background; candidate scoring based on survival differences compared to EV controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNAseq of worms treated with sub-lethal actin knockdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform transcriptome analysis of animals treated with a non-lethal (10% act-1) RNAi to identify genes differentially regulated when actin is perturbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10% act-1 RNAi is chosen because it perturbs actin without affecting growth; sequencing performed at L4 and D1 yielded example outputs (e.g., 450 genes upregulated, 192 downregulated). Use resulting lists to intersect with other screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRISPR-Cas9 screening in human BJ fibroblasts under cytochalasin D
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening to identify genes whose loss increases or decreases susceptibility to the actin-destabilizing agent cytochalasin D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sub-lethal cytochalasin D (e.g., 0.25 µM) treatment, sequencing and sgRNA distribution analysis to call enriched (protective) and depleted (sensitizing) genes (example counts: 363 enriched, 198 depleted). Cross-reference with worm datasets to find conserved regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis / cross-referencing for high-confidence candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize genes appearing across multiple, independent datasets (imaging, synthetic lethality, RNAseq, CRISPR screens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding genes with overlapping function across different screens reveals core nodes (here, chromatin remodeling and lipid homeostasis) and increases confidence in their relevance to actin maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven mechanistic tests for BET-1 and MYST HATs
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether BET-1 and MYST HATs (mys-1, mys-2, etc.) regulate cytoskeletal health via chromatin-mediated transcriptional programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictions and tests include: knockdown of mys-1/ mys-2 should mimic bet-1 knockdown defects; bet-1 knockdown should not further worsen phenotypes in mys-1/2 knockdown if they act in same pathway; test putative MYST HATs C34B7.1/2 as extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: BET-1 localization and ChIP-seq as readouts of transcriptional activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess BET-1 functional activity by tagging endogenous BET-1 with GFP and quantifying nuclear localization across aging, and by performing BET-1 ChIP-seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BET-1::GFP is a validated functional fusion; quantify localization at D1, D4, D7, D10, D13. ChIP-seq will be performed with expert guidance (Dr. Michael Eisen) to directly measure BET-1 binding to actin-regulatory loci and changes with age or genetic perturbation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chromatin accessibility and transcriptome assays (ATAC-seq and RNAseq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ATAC-seq to profile global chromatin accessibility and RNAseq to assess transcriptional changes in animals with altered MYST HATs or lipid-regulator expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATAC-seq adapted for adult C. elegans will be used to understand global chromatin availability; RNAseq performed at Vincent J. Coates Genomics Sequencing Laboratory; data analysis using Galaxy and Matlab with lab bioinformatics support. Look for shared motifs/enhancers among cytoskeletal genes.

rubrics_metrics.name: H4 acetylation measurement by immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess histone H4 acetylation state (targets of MYST HATs) to test whether lipid regulators (e.g., NHR-49, DAF-16) alter acetylation and thereby affect BET-1 binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use H4 immunoprecipitation followed by mass-spec to quantify acetylation at K5, K8, K12, K16; test effects of knockdown or overexpression of nhr-49 and daf-16 on H4 acetylation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lipid measurements using microscopy stains and COPAS biosorter
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure organismal and tissue lipid levels and lipid droplet morphology using BODIPY and Nile Red staining and quantify using fluorescent microscopy, flow cytometry, and COPAS biosorting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether actin perturbations (e.g., act-1 or lev-11 RNAi) increase muscle lipid droplets and whether protecting cytoskeleton prevents age-associated lipid dysregulation. Also test whether proper cytoskeletal function is required for NHR-49/DAF-16 effects on lipid phenotypes (measure β-oxidation and desaturation via qPCR of canonical targets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of pathway epistasis (HSF-1, DAF-16, NHR-49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the epistatic relationships among HSF-1, DAF-16, and NHR-49 in regulating actin homeostasis and lipid metabolism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform overexpression and knockdown combinations: (1) test if hsf-1 overexpression rescues daf-16 or nhr-49 RNAi phenotypes (if not, suggests downstream relationship); (2) test whether neuronal hsf-1 requires daf-16/nhr-49 in peripheral tissue by knockdown and assay for cytoskeletal protection and lifespan extension; (3) use qPCR to validate differential regulation of actin targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess non-autonomous signaling by tissue-specific overexpression
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether transcription factors (HSF-1, NHR-49, DAF-16, BET-1) can signal non-autonomously from neurons to protect peripheral tissue cytoskeleton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overexpress genes in neurons (e.g., rab-3p::hsf-1) and test distal tissue actin, lipid content, and lifespan; perform H4 acetylation assays, ATAC-seq, BET-1 localization/ChIP-seq to probe mechanism; test requirement of bet-1/mys-1/mys-2 by RNAi to see if they suppress neuronal hsf-1 benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate controls and explicit caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ empty vector (EV) controls, non-lethal perturbation doses, and plan caveat/alternative experiments to interpret negative or ambiguous results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: EV controls shown for cytoskeletal integrity comparisons; 10% act-1 RNAi chosen to perturb actin without affecting growth; recognize RNAi may produce stronger phenotypes than chronic lof due to adaptation, so include CRISPR null confirmation; if overexpression does not extend lifespan, perform complementary knockdown/lof experiments to probe mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of actin phenotypes with organismal physiology
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate measured actin structural/dynamic changes with physiological outcomes like lifespan and stress resistance to infer functional significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example predictions: bet-1 knockdown should produce premature cytoskeletal breakdown and shortened lifespan; overexpression should protect actin late in life and extend lifespan unless effects are actin-independent (test via actin regulator knockdown). Quantitative actin metrics will be correlated with lifespan and lipid phenotypes.
